rationale:
Evidence: all 60 development trials across five designs ended off_track with zero completions. Progress ranged from 0.04 to 0.17, and max_error sat at 0.06 to 0.067, just past the 0.06 m limit. Scores were nearly identical across iterations 0, 1, 3 and 5 (about 39.85), so gain scale and sensor size alone are not moving the result. Iteration 2, which widened the spacing and lowered kp, was worst, so under-steering with a coarse array is also wrong. The common pattern is a robot that leaves the line early, with 1 to 2 line-loss events and steering oscillation of 0.06 to 0.18 in every run.

Changes: (1) Sensors move forward to y = 0.06 m, the far end of the allowed range. Reading the line further ahead gives the loop lookahead and cuts the phase lag that drives overshoot. 7 sensors at 0.01 m spacing across x = -0.03 to +0.03 m keep the smooth signal from iterations 3 and 5. (2) sensor_size 0.016, so the tape stays under at least one sensor at the outer offsets and line-loss events drop. (3) Weights stay a linear ramp from -1 to +1. (4) kp 4.0 to 3.0, a moderate reduction to ease overshoot now that lookahead is added. (5) kd 0.8 to 1.0 to damp oscillation. (6) ki 0.0 to avoid windup. (7) wheel_track 0.12 to 0.14. A wider track lowers the yaw rate per unit of wheel difference, which reduces the effective steering gain and the oscillation. (8) mass 0.6 kept. (9) base_speed 1.3 to 1.5 to keep a realistic chance of finishing in 3 s, since 1.0 and 1.3 gave little progress.

Expected result: a modest gain over the 39.85 baseline, through fewer line-loss events and a longer run on the line. Completion is still uncertain. The main risk is that the forward sensor and wider track change the response in a way the telemetry does not yet show, so the Evaluator should check whether the change in lookahead is large enough to matter.
